description: One read of the Atlas repository at a pinned commit, recorded so the guide's claim about the ChatGPT and Claude bootstrap routes can be checked offline. The claim this supports is the sentence in docs/how-to-help-shoggoth.md that says those two routes are covered by the Atlas launcher tests. Nothing here is generated; it is a transcript of the read named under `read`, and re-reading it is the way to refresh it.

read.network: read once, here; no test reads the network

route_test.block_sha256_over: The 16 block lines joined by a newline, with no trailing newline. The obvious re-derivation keeps the trailing newline and returns db590ad55812e1b05744160631578125b0f769425ba74d4e6b79635fd88d581a over the same 16 lines, so a reader who gets that digest has met this convention rather than the wrong file. Every other identifier here reproduces with the obvious command: file_sha256 is the sha256 of the whole file, and each test_files blob is the git blob id the read returned.
route_test.cited_as: lines 98 to 114 in the 2026-09-05 runbook amendment, which counts the blank line above the block
route_test.test_name_template: ${provider} redirect carries the API-selected issue and prompt

conclusion.claim_supported: Both bootstrap routes carry a test at this commit, so the guide sentence saying the ChatGPT and Claude routes are covered by the Atlas launcher tests is true as written.
conclusion.not_established: A passing route test says the redirect is built correctly. It says nothing about what the browser chat behind the redirect can do, which is why the guide's next sentence limits the claim to a bootstrap.
